newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C. Bank raises borrowing rate to 10.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila C. Bank raises borrowing rate to 10.25 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Friday it had raised its overnight borrowing rate to 10.25 percent from 10.0 percent.
But it left its overnight lending rate at 12.65 percent.
"We just want to realign it with the rates. The T-bill rates had been going up," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters.
"We had been waiting for the Central Bank to raise its rate," a foreign bank dealer. "It had been delaying it, but the final trigger was the weakness in the peso."
Traders said the Central Bank had been forced to unload over $100 million on Thursday to assuage an edgy market over talks that the Philippines may suffer the same fate as Thailand.
Philippine banks may be hit hard in case the property sector experiences a downturn.
This has led banks to buy dollars to meet the needs of foreign investors who may decide to leave the Philippines, they said.
